shared_gate: Every controller for the admitted route must use the SAME coordinator gate G. Hold G across admission, allowance count, prior-operation check, durable intent reservation, token validation, request and confirmation. Acquire, release and reclaim must also use G. Similar or nested-but-separate mutexes do not provide this transaction.

repros.name: Admission/reservation race
repros.setup: A and B share journal J, lease identity L and a valid fixture token.
repros.sequence: Pause A after no-prior-intent or used=0. B reserves the same operation and loses its reply, or completes another operation under the shared one-action allowance. Resume A.
repros.observed: A also dispatches, duplicating the operation or exceeding the allowance.
repros.expected: Competing work is rejected before transport; unresolved operations remain blocked.

repros.name: Transfer during an acting request
repros.setup: A owns LA; lease object B references the same identity.
repros.sequence: A validates and enters fake transport; pause before the fake effect. Through B, release LA and acquire LB. Resume A.
repros.observed: Takeover completes, then A acts with invalid LA.
repros.expected: A completes while still owner before transfer, or is fenced before effect. An exception or unknown request result must not automatically make takeover safe.

first_supported_profile: Qualify one owned process and imported module first. One coordinator owns G, L and J; all controllers and lease transitions use its handles. Reject inconsistent bindings and unbound input; define a canonical route/state identity. Prohibit independent cross-process dispatch/takeover in this profile. A module registry is not interprocess coordination. Restart requires renewed admission and reconciliation; recovered journal state does not grant authority.
uncertainty: Retain ownership through the potentially acting request. Preserve durable uncertainty and hold unsafe transfer until trusted reconciliation establishes quiescence.
unchanged_prerequisites: Trusted task/version/target/session/payload admission, fresh identity/focus checks, budgets and uncertainty safeguards remain mandatory after the mutex patch.
cleanup: Close every successful-response object in finally, including read exceptions and overflow; preserve passing normal-success and bounded HTTP-error behavior.
scope: Sanitized synthetic repair specifications from the completed review; no new execution or source changes for this supplement. This is a bounded source patch/qualification contract, not live-use approval.
